te.title: Oil off spec in the evening
te.sit: Oil treating complains that your oil is wet: their sample shows more than 1 % water. On your DCS the interface LI-120 is on set point, the temperature is normal and nothing was changed on the unit this shift.

te.title: Flaring with a normal pressure
te.sit: The flare operator reports a steady flame from your unit. Your PI-110 reads 9.8 bar g, a little below set point, and FI-117 shows about 11 kSm³/h. K-201 is running.

te.title: Liquid in the compressor scrubber
te.sit: Gas compression reports liquid collecting in the K-201 suction scrubber. The well rates and the separator levels have not changed. PDI-113 has risen over the last half hour.

te.title: Water outlet opening up
te.sit: LIC-120 has been opening LV-120 for half an hour (now above 75 %) while FI-123 is almost unchanged. The water treatment header pressure is normal. The oil-in-water is creeping up.

te.title: Interface steady, water dirty
te.sit: Water treatment says your water is oily and their hydrocyclones are overloaded. LI-120 sits on its 550 mm set point. LV-120 opened wide for a while (FI-123 peaked above 30 m³/h) and is now back near its normal output.

te.title: High carry-over after a well change
te.sit: Liquid carry-over FI-119 is in alarm. The oil and water rates are normal, the levels are on set point, PV-110 is 90 % open and PDI-113 is higher than usual.

te.title: Level reads high but no alarm on the interface
te.sit: LI-125 has risen by about 250 mm and is noisy; LI-120 and LI-130 are normal. FI-119 carry-over is in alarm. Nothing was changed.

te.title: Wet oil on a cold morning
te.sit: BS&W has risen to about 0.8 % and is still rising. TIC-102 is below its set point and in alarm. The demulsifier pump is running at its normal rate.

te.title: Bucket climbing toward the weir
te.sit: LI-130 swings with the flowline and reaches about 850 mm on the liquid surges. LIC-130 output reaches 100 % on the surges although the oil flow is only slightly above normal.

te.title: Flare flame at night, all controllers normal
te.sit: The night shift sees a small flame at the flare. PIC-111 output is 0 %, BDV-118 is closed, the pressure is on set point and K-201 is running. FI-117 reads about 0.8 kSm³/h.

te.title: Water in the oil after a rate increase
te.sit: BS&W has jumped above 1 % over the last half hour. LIC-120 output is climbing steadily; FI-123 has not moved from 20 m³/h. Production reports higher water from a well.

te.title: Pressure rising and flaring after the lunch break
te.sit: The pressure jumped to 11 bar g, FI-117 reads about 11 kSm³/h and FI-116 is zero. PV-110 is wide open.

meta.title: Troubleshooting report — TE-1 Oil off spec in the evening (Three-Phase Separator V-101)
meta.caseTitle: Oil off spec in the evening
meta.sit: Oil treating complains that your oil is wet: their sample shows more than 1 % water. On your DCS the interface LI-120 is on set point, the temperature is normal and nothing was changed on the unit this shift.

0.1.unit: V-101 is a horizontal three-phase separator (2.0 m × 6.0 m) at 10.0 bar g and 50 °C. The well stream from the production manifold (40 m³/h oil, 20 m³/h water, 12 kSm³/h gas) passes the choke HV-100, receives demulsifier from P-105 (FIC-105, 0.8 L/h = 20 ppm), is heated in E-101 (TIC-102 50 °C) and separates in V-101: gas to K-201, oil over the weir into the bucket and to the LP separator (LIC-130), water to the hydrocyclones (LIC-120 holds the interface at 550 mm). The oil must leave with BS&W below 1 vol%, the water with less than 1000 mg/L oil.

rows.what: Oil treating's sample shows more than 1 % water in our oil (oil treating's call at 00:21:30: about 1.5 %)
AI-132 BS&W 1.24 vol% at 00:20:00 (design 0.51); AI-132 HI first at 00:16:53
LI-120 554 mm on its 550 mm set point; TI-102 50.0 °C on 50 °C
Standing alarms: FI-105 LO and P-105 STOP since 00:01:01, AI-132 HI since 00:17:04
AI-122 oil in water 660 mg/L (design 494), rising

0.4.ctx: Evening shift, wells at the normal choke (HIC-100 50 %). The shift report says nothing was changed on the unit. Normal state: BS&W ≈ 0.5 vol%, OiW ≈ 500 mg/L, interface 550 mm, 50 °C, demulsifier 0.8 L/h.

R.1.p: Gravity separation: in the inlet section water drops settle down through the oil pad and oil drops rise through the water layer while the liquid flows towards the weir. A drop is removed if it can cross its layer in the residence time. Demulsifier (P-105) and heat (E-101) make the drops coalesce into bigger ones; without them the drops stay small, an emulsion (rag) layer builds at the interface and water is carried over the weir with the oil. LIC-120 holds the interface; the oil pad above it and the water layer below it set the two residence times.

R.2.eq: v_t = g·d²·(ρ_w − ρ_o) / (18·μ_o);  a drop is removed if v_t ≥ h_o / τ_o, i.e. d ≥ d_c = √(18·μ_o·h_o / (g·Δρ·τ_o))

sym.m: Terminal settling velocity of a water drop in the oil (Stokes)
Drop diameter; smallest drop that is removed
Water and oil density (1010 and 810 kg/m³ at design)
Oil viscosity (0.9 cP at 50 °C; higher when colder)
Oil pad height the drop must cross; oil residence time (≈ 7.7 min at design)

AI-132 1.24 vol% and rising about 0.07 vol% per minute

1.3.safn: Pressure 10.00 bar g (PSHH 11.5); levels in band; no trip is approaching
1.3.envn: Oil in water 660 mg/L and rising; limit 1000 mg/L to the hydrocyclones (the no-action reference run passes it at 00:38:00)
1.3.eqn: No machine or vessel limit involved
1.3.prodn: Off-spec oil: training penalty 25 USD/m³ × 39 m³/h ≈ USD 975 per hour while BS&W > 1 %
1.3.ttl: ≈ 18 min to the OiW limit if nothing is done; BS&W rising ≈ 0.07 vol%/min

1.4.why: No safety limit is near; shutting in the wells would cost far more than the off-spec penalty. The oil-in-water is the clock: about 20 min to the hydrocyclone limit, so diagnose quickly and slow the rise meanwhile.
1.4.park: Stop the rapid change: TIC-102 SP 50 → 55 °C (heat lowers the oil viscosity). Stop line: AI-122 > 1000 mg/L or AI-132 > 2.5 % → call the supervisor and cut the choke.

1.5.sp: A reduced, stable condition that stops the problem growing while you investigate (for example more heat, a lower rate, a controller in MAN).
1.5.tc: A consequence (safety, environment, equipment) arrives before the diagnosis is finished unless you act now.

1.6.p: Stokes settling in the oil pad: a water drop is removed only if g·d²·Δρ/(18·μ_o) ≥ h_o/τ_o — the drop size d (set by demulsifier and heat) matters most, as d².

3.2.n: Liquid balance closes (in 60.0 m³/h at design rates; out 39.0 + 20.6 m³/h): no extra liquid. Water leaving with the oil: 1.24 % × 39.0 m³/h = 0.48 m³/h against 0.20 m³/h at design. The DCS cut size d_c is 97 µm against 97 µm at design, so the residence time is unchanged — the drops themselves must be smaller.

Rates at design; no hidden extra liquid

3.5.tree:
TOP: water in the oil above 1 % with the interface and temperature normal
 OR — drops too small to settle (emulsion)
     OR — no demulsifier (P-105 stopped / line blocked)
     OR — demulsifier ineffective (wrong chemical)
     OR — colder feed (heater)
 OR — less settling time (more liquid, more water)
 OR — oil pad thinner than shown (LT-120 reads low)
 OR — water bypasses the pad (internals)
 OR — the measurement is high (AI-132)
3.5.cut: Single-element cut sets: {no demulsifier}, {wrong chemical}, {colder feed}, {more liquid}, {more water}, {LT-120 low}, {internals}, {AI-132 high}. No AND gate is needed: each path alone gives the top event.

rows.how: Killed by the lab (1.50 %) and oil treating (≈ 1.5 %)

rows.st: “Nothing was changed on the unit this shift.”
rows.how: True for deliberate changes; the alarm log shows P-105 stopped at 0:01

3.8.n: No deliberate change was made, but the alarm log shows P-105 STOP at 00:01:01. The BS&W began to rise about 7 min later and slowly — the time an emulsion needs to tighten once the chemical is gone. The timing fits a lost demulsifier, not a step change of the interface or the rate.

3.10.n: None — the team agrees that drop size (chemical and heat) and the oil-pad residence time decide the BS&W

3.11.n: Nothing in Explore contradicts the statement; it names no cause and stays valid

Demulsifier tank T-105 empty
Wrong demulsifier delivered
LT-120 reads low after maintenance
Heater short of steam
Well watering out
Weir plate damaged

rows.act: Do not move the interface set point to “fix” the BS&W
rows.why: Lowering LIC-120 thins the water layer and drives the OiW over its limit

rows.act: Do not shut in the wells
rows.why: Not time-critical; a shutdown costs far more than the penalty

Confirms WH-1 and kills WH-7; reversible, cheap

5.1.proof: Ev-1, Ev-4 (FI-105 0, P-105 STOP); T-1 rag band; T-2 bottle test; T-3 BS&W ↓ after restart (control run kept rising)
5.1.mech: P-105 stopped at 00:01:00 (SIS message “Demulsifier pump P-105 tripped”) → no demulsifier in the well stream → the water drops stop coalescing: the DCS cut size stays at ≈ 97 µm but more of the drops are smaller than that → an emulsion (rag) band grows at the interface (108 mm at 20 min) and LT-120 reads the middle of it → water drops are carried over the weir with the oil: BS&W 0.51 → 1.24 vol% at 20 min, and oil drops stay in the water: OiW 494 → 660 mg/L.

rows.opt: Restart P-105 at 0.8 L/h and hold TIC-102 at 55 °C until BS&W < 1 %, then back to 50 °C
Raise TIC-102 only and live with the stopped pump
Lower LIC-120 to thicken the oil pad
DCS alarm on demulsifier dose in ppm (FI-105 / FI-133) plus a standby pump with auto-start

rows.step: Reset and restart P-105 at the Field tab (FIC-105 AUTO 0.80 L/h)
Hold TIC-102 at 55 °C until AI-132 < 1 %, then return it to 50 °C
If P-105 trips again: electrician to check the motor and the overload relay
Add a dose alarm (ppm) and a standby pump study
Tell oil treating and water treatment when back on spec

rows.act: Alarms acknowledged; telephone to oil treating; samples to the lab
P-105 START at the Field tab (FIC-105 AUTO, SP 0.80 L/h)

5.7.n: None: AI-132 HI cleared for good at 00:31:15, BS&W 0.39 % at 0:45:00 and 0.44 % at 1:00:00 after TIC-102 went back to 50 °C; OiW 451 mg/L; LG-121 sharp again at 1:00:00.

5.8.rule: When the oil goes wet with the interface on set point, check that the demulsifier is flowing (FI-105, P-105) and look at LG-121 for a rag band before you touch LIC-120.

6.0.n: Every prediction came true: T-1 no glass interface above LI-120, T-2 lab above 1 %, T-3 BS&W ↓ (1.78 → 0.53 %), the fix back on spec.

rows.m: DCS alarm on demulsifier dose in ppm (FI-105 / FI-133 × 1000) below 10 ppm
Standby dosing pump with auto-start on P-105 trip (study, MOC)
Shift check of LG-121 for a rag band and of the T-105 tank level

6.1.kpi: Demulsifier dose in ppm and the rag band thickness on LG-121, each shift

rows.i: Back on spec: the margin rose from USD 18,183/h at 0:20 to USD 19,847/h at 1:00 (design ≈ 19,771)
The hydrocyclones never reached their oil-in-water limit
An auto-start spare pump can hide a pump that keeps tripping — alarm the auto-start too

hz.cause: P-105 trip, T-105 empty, suction or discharge valve closed
hz.sg: New dose alarm (ppm); standby pump auto-start; T-105 level alarm

hz.dev: MORE demulsifier flow (auto-start of both pumps)
hz.cause: Spare starts while the duty pump runs
hz.cons: Overdosing: hazy water (bottle test), chemical cost
hz.sg: Run interlock duty/standby; FI-105 HI alarm

6.3.fut: A chemical that the separation depends on deserves the same alarms as a level or a pressure: alarm the dose, not only the pump.

6.4.how: Margin of this run against the no-action reference run over the hour (USD 785) plus the difference at 1:00 (USD 1,333/h) for the rest of an 8-hour shift (7 h, assumed). Training prices of the page.

6.5.again:
Read the alarm log first: the first alarm (FI-105 LO / P-105 STOP) came 16 minutes before the BS&W alarm.
Compare every level transmitter with its gauge glass when the quality is off.
Use a cheap, reversible trial (restart the pump) with a control run in mind.
6.5.never:
Never move the interface set point to fix wet oil before knowing why.
Never accept “it is the analyzer again” without a sample.

hyp.cat: Well stream & feed (rates, water cut, gas, sand)

hyp.key: FI-133 and FI-123 above design; choke opened
hyp.fals: FI-133 40 and FI-123 20 m³/h; HIC-100 at 50 %

hyp.cause: AI-132 analyzer reads high (the oil is really dry)
hyp.cat: Instruments & control (LT, PT, analyzers, loops, valves)
hyp.ifthen: If the analyzer drifted, a sample taken by hand shows BS&W below 1 %
hyp.fals: Lab and oil treating also find > 1 %

hyp.cause: Weir or oil bucket internals damaged: water reaches the bucket
hyp.cat: Separator internals (diverter, weir, bucket, mesh pad)
hyp.ifthen: If an internal path lets water into the bucket, BS&W is high whatever the chemistry and the temperature
hyp.key: BS&W does not respond to demulsifier or heat; LG-131 normal
hyp.fals: BS&W falls back to spec when the demulsifier returns

hyp.cause: Demulsifier injected but not working (wrong or spoilt chemical)
hyp.cat: Chemicals & utilities (demulsifier, LP steam, antifoam, air, power)
hyp.ifthen: If the chemical is wrong, FI-105 shows the normal 0.8 L/h but the emulsion still tightens
hyp.key: FI-105 normal; bottle test fails even with fresh chemical
hyp.fals: FI-105 is zero — nothing is injected at all

tests.title: Field check: gauge glass LG-121 against LI-120, and pump P-105
tests.move: Field tab ▸ gauge glasses and the P-105 card at 0:20:00. Nothing is changed on the plant.

WH-1.note: glass interface near LI-120 but with a thick rag band; P-105 stopped

WH-2.note: glass interface ABOVE LI-120 (the real interface is higher than the reading)

tests.kill: If the glass interface is not above LI-120 → WH-2 killed; a rag band thicker than about 50 mm and P-105 stopped → WH-1 supported.

res.obs: LG-121 interface 524 mm with a rag band 108 mm thick; LI-120 554 mm reads inside the band, 30 mm above the glass interface. P-105 STOPPED.

tests.title: Samples to the lab (centrifuge BS&W, bottle test) and a call to oil treating
tests.move: Field tab ▸ Take samples and Telephones ▸ Oil treating at 0:20:00. Nothing is changed on the plant.

WH-1.note: lab BS&W above 1 % like AI-132; bottle test does not break without extra demulsifier

WH-6.note: lab BS&W below 1 % — AI-132 reads high

tests.kill: Lab BS&W above 1 % → WH-6 killed; bottle test breaks cleanly at the present dose → WH-1 weakened.

res.obs: Oil treating 00:21:30: about 1.5 % water. Lab 00:22:00: BS&W 1.50 vol%, water 705 mg/L, water cut 33 %, bottle test: no break in 10 min without more demulsifier.

tests.title: Restart P-105 at 0.8 L/h (trial fix) and watch AI-132
tests.move: Field ▸ P-105 START at 0:26:00; FIC-105 left in AUTO at 0.80 L/h; TIC-102 held at 55 °C since 0:22:10; nothing else touched; hold 10 min.

WH-1.note: BS&W below 1 % within about 10 min as the dose reaches the drops; rag band thins

WH-7.note: a damaged weir or bucket passes water whatever the chemistry

tests.kill: If AI-132 falls by more than 0.3 vol% within 10 min → WH-7 killed and WH-1 confirmed; if it keeps rising as in the heat-only control run (1.78 → 2.34 %) → WH-1 killed.
tests.stop: Stop and call the supervisor if AI-122 > 1000 mg/L, LI-120 leaves 350–800 mm or AI-132 passes 2.5 %

res.obs: FI-105 back to 0.79 L/h within 1 min (FI-105 LO cleared). AI-132 1.78 → 0.53 vol% in 10 min; AI-132 HI cleared for good at 00:31:15, 5 min after the restart. Control run (heat only): 1.78 → 2.34 vol%.
